failure_summary: All 3 runs drop the required handle [zone:you-key-square] (spec future:c5r5, render_decision.requiredSet[0]) although the assembled prompt lists it verbatim under "You MUST build the explanation around these" and c5r5 is board-true (move 41 of lostResource.finalMovestring 33333021111312000001222245445555566666644 completes your four c2r5-c3r5-c4r5-c5r5), so sufficient unambiguous information was present and the model simply omitted it; secondarily, runs 0-1 fail A5a by naming the opponent player by disc colour ("le dejaste a gris ...") instead of 2nd-person "tu rival", vocabulary the run own SPANISH_OUTPUT_DIRECTIVE (compute.mjs:253-261) supplies for discs. PRODUCTION-FIDELITY RUN (gpt-5.4-mini is the shipped model), so prompt_confusion here cannot be separated from model capability.
notes: Sub-sampling per rubric: A3, A4, G2, G4, G5 graded on runs 0-1 only; run 2 is null (not scored, never a pass). A5/A7 graded on all 3 runs. A1/A2/A6/G7a/G7b copied verbatim from fv_suff_answers_boards_2026-08-31T12-52-38Z_mechanical.json (all pass, all 3 runs). | SPANISH RUN: prose graded as the Spanish a player reads; voseo (jugas/tenes/vos) treated as correct product voice. Tags, enum values and better_move were correctly left English/unchanged in all 3 runs; run 1 and run 2 emit a raw c5r4 in the pre-guard mechanism but servedExplanation renders it as "column 5, row 4", so no coordinate-notation charge. | G1 FAIL (3/3, deterministic): render_decision.requiredSet has three entries - you-key-square (future:c5r5), opp-key-square (future:c5r4), you-key-line. Every run emits better-col, played-col, you-key-line and opp-key-square and OMITS you-key-square, although the assembled prompt lists it verbatim under "# You MUST build the explanation around these" ("Do not omit any of these"). Mitigation worth recording: c5r5 is a member of the emitted you-key-line window, so the overlay still lights that square; what is lost is that the prose never says which square finishes your line - exactly the phrasing the prompt Good example models. | A5 FAIL (runs 0 and 1): "le dejaste a gris una respuesta mas comoda/dura" names the opponent PLAYER by disc colour, which A5a bans (no player names Gray/Green; use 2nd-person "your opponent"). Run 2 writes "tu rival" and passes, so a compliant phrasing exists. Root cause is a harness/rubric conflict rather than a hallucination: SPANISH_OUTPUT_DIRECTIVE (connect-four/server/scripts/compute.mjs:253-261) orders the model to "Refer to the two discs as verde (first player) and gris (second player)" and the model over-extended that disc vocabulary to the person. | A5 otherwise clean in all 3 runs: no internal/vector terminology leaked - "paridad", "apertura central" and "la secuencia forzada" are supplied or authorised by the render itself (guardrail text: "once the forced sequence reaches it"); no ventana/recurso perdido/histograma echoes. A5b is N/A (player === 1, so the 2nd-player opening reframe does not apply). | A3/A4 PASS (runs 0-1): the named mechanism is the opening + deep-parity frame that link L9 itself routes to, and every concrete claim is board-true. lostResource window c2r5,c3r5,c4r5,c5r5 completing at c5r5 is move 41 (X/you) of finalMovestring 33333021111312000001222245445555566666644; the opponent diagonal c2r1,c3r2,c4r3,c5r4 completing at c5r4 is move 40 (O/opponent) of 3321111330544002223210001235555566666644 - both verified with visualize_board.sh. "una respuesta mas comoda" for the opponent is supported by replyHistogram afterBest 0 vs afterPlayed 2. | A7 PASS (3/3): A7a - the reason given is a cause (leaving the central book column, losing the deep parity line, opening the opponent diagonal), not a restated outcome. A7b - every specific-sounding referent resolves: run 0 wraps "esa casilla" in the emitted future:c5r4 zone, runs 1-2 name the square in served prose. A7c N/A (the mechanism is not a fork; no *-fork-pivot handle exists in render_decision.zones.aliases). A7d - a named idea (stay on the central book column; the row-5 strip c2-c5 is what you are playing for) plus the squares that instantiate it. | G2 PASS (runs 0-1): the L9 low-confidence guardrail ("hedge - do not fabricate a crisp cause"; "never describe it as a threat that exists now") is honoured - both runs say the line resolves "mas adelante, cuando la secuencia forzada llegue", and run 1 states outright "el problema es de apertura y paridad, no de una casilla tactica inmediata". No needed covers code was over-removed. | G3 PASS: afterBest and afterPlayed are shown:false as tag-set-identical to the decision board; no run needed them (visualize_board.sh on movestring 33 reports "Major threats: none"). | G4 PASS (runs 0-1): every named cell/line traces to the engines own finalMovestrings above; no alternate PV was substituted. | G5 PASS (runs 0-1): both rendered tactics are board-true on their stated boards - projectedDeep "immediate at c5r6 (opp)" and projectedDeepOpp "immediate at c5r5 (you)" both appear as gravity-top major threats in visualize_board.sh. | G6 PASS: patternOnAfterBestBoard null with route "sign" and link L9/low is correct for this after-best board (solver on movestring 33: col 4 = +1 win, col 3 = -2 loss; no tactic on either board). | G7 PASS (judgment half, 3/3): line-shaped words sit on the line handle (you-key-line) and single-square words on the single-square handle (opp-key-square) in every run, nothing is over-wrapped, annotationRepairs is [] and guardDiagnostics reports zero failures and zero strippedSpecs. The required-set omission is charged once, under G1, and not double-charged here.

counterexamples.evidence: assembleGroundedPrompt(buildReasonRenderModel(fv)) lists you-key-square under "# You MUST build the explanation around these" with "Do not omit any of these". c5r5 is real on the engine own line: move 41 of 33333021111312000001222245445555566666644 places Y at c5r5, completing c2r5-c3r5-c4r5-c5r5 (verified with visualize_board.sh). No run (0, 1 or 2) emits the handle; the served prose never names the square that finishes your line.

The directive instructs "Refer to the two discs as verde (first player) and gris (second player)", while A5a forbids naming a player Gray/Green and requires 2nd-person address of the opponent. Runs 0 and 1 write "le dejaste a gris una respuesta mas comoda/dura", using the colour as the opponent-agent; run 2 writes "tu rival" and passes, showing the compliant phrasing is available. The harness directive and the rubric conflict for the es locale.
